content.comment_body: Hello, I have two issues with [product_name] Soft Comfort: First, the application display resolution isn't right. Even after adjusting my screen settings, the text remains very small and hard to read. I've attached a screenshot for reference. Second, I'm unable to link the software to my [product_name] PLC series. I've tried connecting the PLC using its IP address via Ethernet, but it doesn't work. Any advice?

What operating system are you using? Which [product_name] Soft Comfort version is installed? Which [product_name] PLC model do you have ([article_no])? What is your PC/laptop's IP address? What is its subnet mask? What is the PLC's IP address and subnet mask?

-Windows 10 -[version_no] -[article_no] -My PC's IP address: 192.168.1.3 -PC subnet mask: 255.255.255.0 -PLC IP: 169.254.25.72 -PLC subnet: 255.255.0.0 Just realized, do I need a router to connect to my PLC? Currently, I'm connecting it directly to my computer without a router.

Hi [user_name], Could you try something simple: PC IP: 192.168.0.1 Subnet: 255.255.255.0 PLC IP: 192.168.0.2 Subnet: 255.255.255.0 This setup works since both devices must be on the same subnet for communication. Also, be sure to select the correct LAN adapter when transferring data. My PC is set at 1920x1080 resolution and the display seems fine. Regards

The PC and PLC need to be in the same IP address range. For example, the first three parts of their IP addresses should match, but the last part should be different. If your PC is 192.168.1.3, set your PLC to 192.168.1.4. Make sure their subnet masks are identical.
Please upload your screenshot directly to the forum. For security reasons, I prefer not to follow external links.

Thanks for your suggestions. I tried everything mentioned, but it's still not working. Even with the right IP configured on the PLC, my PC detects a different one. I also tried connecting through a router—tested with two routers, but neither detected the PLC, as if it was off. Also, does [product_name] Soft Comfort V8 detect the PLC automatically when on the network? I tried entering the IP address manually in the settings, but when I click OK, nothing happens and the software doesn't start searching for the PLC.

Try connecting the PLC directly to your PC, without a router. You can set the PLC's IP address and subnet mask manually using its display. Is your PC's IP address static or dynamic? Please share screenshots of IP settings for both PLC and PC.
Hello [user_name], For monitor resolution, I recommend using 1920 x 1080. Best regards

Check your PC’s antivirus software—it may block external communication. Try disabling it and see if that helps. Also, verify which LAN adapter you are using and please provide screenshots of both sides’ IP settings, which will help us understand the problem better.

Hi, 1. [product_name] Soft Comfort V8 isn't officially supported on Windows 10 2. Make sure Java is updated 3. Run the software as administrator 4. Try: - Connect the PLC directly to the PC with an Ethernet cable - Disconnect all other Ethernet connections (WiFi, etc.) - Start [product_name] Soft Comfort (LSC) - Click Upload - Ensure only one Ethernet card shows up (refer to attached picture) - Press the scan button (refer to picture) After a while you should be prompted to continue. Once done, the PLC’s IP should appear so you can select it. If this works, check the IP addresses of all devices to avoid conflicts. If needed, set a unique unused IP in the same subnet for the PLC, reconnect it to your network, and retry. It works in Windows 7; hopefully, it will also work in Windows 10. Good luck

I tried setting the resolution to 1920x1080 but the application still shows tiny text. I also uninstalled the antivirus and disabled the firewall, but there's still no change. My PC configuration is attached. My laptop doesn’t have a built-in Ethernet port, so I use an adapter connected through USB. My PC recognizes the Ethernet connections thanks to drivers.
Here is the PLC configuration screenshot (attached).
The scan button doesn’t seem to function. I click it, but nothing happens (see attached screen).

Hi, In your last dialog screenshot, press the "Agenda" button. Enter the PLC's IP, correct subnet, and a name for it. After closing and reopening, press "collega". You should then see a green check mark. If not, open a command prompt (search for CMD in the Windows Start menu). Type: ping [PLC IP address] and press ENTER You should see feedback like in the picture. If the ping fails, your PC can't reach the PLC. This means your PC's Ethernet settings may be incorrect. Hope this helps.
That’s what I tried, but in the "Agenda" dialog, I can’t enter the IP address. Clicking or typing does nothing—I’m unable to input anything.

Hi, I’m not confident Windows 10 is reliable for this task. Have you tried another Windows version to establish PLC communication? At the moment, there isn’t a clear baseline, so many things could be wrong. The dialog you showed is for setting up the communication link. Your interface is set to the Wi-Fi card. As a start, consider using a direct connection. Getting the basics set up is important. If you use Wi-Fi, try connecting without gateway settings first. Otherwise, check what gateway is set on the PLC. The "Agenda" button is called "Address Book" in English. To the left of this button is a field where you can type in the IP address. If this doesn’t work, see if you can run the application as administrator in Windows 10. Sorry I can’t offer more—the goal is to keep troubleshooting and move the discussion forward.

Hi, - Run [product_name] Soft Comfort V8 as administrator! - Connect the [product_name] module directly to your PC Ethernet card with a cable! - Disable all other Ethernet adapters so you can only select one! - Add the PLC IP and press the TEST button. - If you see a green check mark, the issue is likely with Ethernet (address conflict or subnet difference). If your PC Ethernet adapter uses another subnet, [product_name] Soft Comfort will automatically adjust as needed (works for Windows 7). If you still can't find the PLC, Windows 10 may not be supported. Try running the software in Windows 7 compatibility mode—it might help. Hope this helps.

I followed the advice from [user_name] and [user_name], and here are my results (attached): The PLC seems to be recognized—the status label says "yes"—but back in the "Agenda" dialog, the TEST button remains greyed out. At this point, I suspect a Windows 10 incompatibility. What do you think?

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced two major problems with [product_name] Soft Comfort V8.0 on Windows 10: very small and hard-to-read text due to display scaling, and persistent Ethernet connectivity trouble between the PC and a [product_name] PLC module. Multiple attempts to adjust resolution settings and network configurations failed to resolve these issues. There is also uncertainty about whether device discovery should be automatic and about necessary network topology. The feedback demonstrates usability concerns related to application readability and ongoing technical obstacles with core PLC connectivity.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] Soft Comfort to render readable text and reliably connect to and identify their [product_name] PLC over Ethernet, either automatically or with straightforward manual configuration.
